claims.text: Intermediate thermal aging produces a transient brittle regime in FCC/B2 eutectic HEAs.
The transient brittle regime is driven by a percolating network of highly ordered B2 domains.
Highly ordered B2 domains pin dislocations through a frictional mechanism.
Higher aging temperatures disrupt the ordered B2 network through coarsening or disordering and thereby restore ductility.
The initial alloy has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic microstructure.
The B2 phase in the as-cast state is disordered or only partially ordered.
Aging at approximately 500–700 °C is sufficient to drive LCO evolution and B2 coarsening.
Impurity segregation at grain boundaries is absent under the proposed conditions.
Aging changes B2 from a partially ordered state to a highly ordered state with greater lattice-parameter mismatch and chemical disparity.
Lattice-parameter differences and chemical disparity can create a rough energy landscape that hinders defect or partial-dislocation motion.
Increased friction on partial-dislocation motion causes dislocation pinning and brittle fracture in the FCC/B2 alloy.
B2 coarsening lowers interface density, while B2 disordering lowers friction, allowing dislocation glide to resume.
Ductility should evolve non-monotonically from high in the as-cast state, to near zero at peak ordering, and then recover after longer or hotter aging.
The as-cast fine-lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic alloy combines high strength and ductility through composite strengthening and dislocation pinning.
The embrittlement regime is the temperature interval in which B2 local chemical order is maximal but significant coarsening and phase decomposition have not yet occurred.
Sigma-phase formation is an excluded alternative associated with grain-boundary embrittlement.
The exact temperature of peak frictional pinning depends on alloy-specific ordering kinetics and is not established.
The proposed mechanism assumes that B2 remains continuous and does not transform into a grain-boundary sigma phase.
Failure to observe increased LCO during the ductility loss would falsify the ordering-based mechanism.
Embrittlement in the absence of a percolating ordered-domain network would falsify the proposed network mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention says intermediate aging is sufficient to cause B2 coarsening, whereas the stated embrittlement boundary requires maximum ordering without significant coarsening.
